records.text: Our profitability decreased largely as a result of decreased revenue miles per tractor of 7.8%, a 6.3% decrease in available tractors combined with increases in technology and personnel expenses and higher net fuel costs partially offset by an increase in our Brokerage gross margin to 12.6% compared to 8.5% in 2020 on higher Brokerage revenue.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Operating income for 2021 was $18.4 million compared to $43.6 million in 2020.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: The Company’s operating revenue increased by 25.6 percent in 2021 compared to 2020.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: The increase resulted primarily from pricing actions, including a 5.9 percent general rate increase taken on January 18, 2021, for customers subject to general rate increases, in addition to increased volumes, terminal expansion and improvements in mix of business.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: The 2021 operating ratio (operating expenses divided by operating revenue) improved to 85.4 percent as compared to 90.1 percent in 2020.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: The increase in 2021 operating income resulted primarily from pricing actions, partially offset by salary and wage increases, higher fuel costs, and higher purchase transportation costs.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: As discussed in “Financial Condition, Liquidity and Capital Resources” below, the Company has in place a revolving credit facility with up to $300 million in availability, plus an accordion feature that provides for an additional $100 million in availability, subject to certain conditions and lender commitments, in addition to its cash flow from operations.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Enterprise operating revenues increased $1,055.9 million, approximately 23%, in the year ended December 31, 2021 compared to 2020.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: •a $126.5 million increase in fuel surcharge revenues resulting from an increase in fuel prices in 2021 compared to 2020 (for example, based on information reported by the U.S. Department of Energy, the average diesel price per gallon in the U.S. increased by 27% between such periods) and an increase in Intermodal volumes, partially offset by a decrease in Truckload volumes; and

records.title: 10-K
records.text: •an $83.9 million increase in Truckload segment revenues (excluding fuel surcharge) driven by improved revenue per truck per week, partially offset by lower volumes due to driver capacity constraints.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Many of the products we purchase, as well as our labor and certain other operating costs, have experienced price increases driven by supply chain constraints and other inflationary impacts.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Enterprise net income increased $193.7 million, approximately 91%, in the year ended December 31, 2021 compared to 2020, primarily due to a $247.0 million increase in income from operations, partially offset by the corresponding increase in income taxes.
